questions.q: Which three types of feedback does the summary describe?
a: Appreciation, coaching and evaluation
Praise, criticism and punishment
Advice, comparison and correction
Evaluation, instruction and warning
questions.why: Lesson 1 separates feedback into appreciation, coaching and evaluation, each with its own purpose.

questions.q: Which kind of feedback should you focus on when you are exhausted after hard work?
a: Gratitude for how you did
Coaching on how to do better
An evaluation against expectations
Advice from a more experienced peer
questions.why: Lesson 1 says that when you are worn out, appreciate your effort rather than look for improvement.

questions.q: What should you think about before reacting to criticism?
a: What the other person intended and what lies behind it
Whether the person has authority over you
How many other people agree with the criticism
Whether the comment was made in front of others
questions.why: Lesson 2 advises considering the giver’s intentions and digging for the issue underneath.

questions.q: What did the 2007 survey of managers reveal about self-assessment?
a: Most rated themselves in the top 10 percent
Most avoided giving feedback to their staff
Most preferred written feedback to spoken
Most had never received any formal training
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the impossible result to show that we cannot see ourselves objectively.

questions.q: What does a growth mindset let you do with criticism?
a: Treat it as a chance to learn and improve
Decide quickly whether it is fair
Protect your self-image from attack
Wait until your feelings have settled
questions.why: Lesson 3 contrasts a fixed view of yourself with seeing feedback as an opportunity to grow.
